matched_capture_comparison.reason: The complete map regeneration refreshed current authored terrain and water material assets as well as foliage, so the large whole-frame delta is not attributable to understory alone.

accepted_findings: The regenerated L_Terminator map loads in PIE and contains seven tagged, non-colliding scanned HISM actors with 1,440 total small-fir and fern instances.
The imported assets are rights-reviewed CC0 structure analogs with explicit materials, validated Nanite support, grounded pivots, and no medium-fir canopy promotion.
Near-bank and forest-floor cover is visibly denser and more continuous than the retained baseline while preserving 360 procedural gap-fill placements.
The project-owned 4,650-instance canopy and the complete 8,000-instance vegetation budget remain present.
Terrain geometry, terrain collision, water geometry, hydraulics, bathymetry, and raft-force inputs were not changed by this ecology slice.
remaining_photoreal_defects: The project-owned adult canopy remains angular, repetitive, and visibly procedural at guide-seat and river-eye distances.
The small firs and ferns are non-native structure analogs; no qualified regional ecology review has accepted their species mix, density, season, or disturbance pattern.
Near-bank ground still lacks sufficient leaf litter, moss, roots, deadwood, wet sediment, microtopography, and continuous wetness transitions.
The foreground river remains too dark and opaque in the candidate captures, while rapid foam, aeration, spray, holes, rollers, and wave trains remain understated or uniform.
The broad bank and cliff surfaces retain smooth or tessellated procedural character because available elevation and imagery do not resolve sub-meter shoreline and geology detail.
Atmospheric depth, horizon lighting, and canopy response remain flat and stylized rather than photographic.
The environment-only canonical views do not validate raft, crew, paddle, water-occlusion, or gameplay readability in the improved bank context.
No measured desktop or VR performance profile has accepted the added Nanite understory population.
required_external_acceptance_gates: A qualified Futaleufu rafting guide accepts route identity, named-rapid readability, scout lines, bank character, hazards, and gameplay sightlines in runnable guide-eye views.
A geospatial reviewer accepts DEM alignment, coordinate transforms, route stationing, shoreline placement, and the declared boundary between sourced terrain and procedural gap fill.
A regional ecologist or qualified environment-art specialist accepts species and structure analog use, density, age classes, season, wetness, disturbance, geology, and ground-cover composition.
A water-VFX and environment-art review accepts water transmission, raft and crew occlusion, waves, holes, rollers, aeration, spray, foam, bank intersections, and close-range asset quality.

Measured hydraulic and bathymetric evidence accepts flow bands, water-surface elevations, velocities, Froude behavior, rapid-specific features, and hazard response without presentation geometry standing in for physics.
Measured full-run desktop and VR profiles pass release frame-time, memory, streaming, shader, stability, and comfort budgets on named target hardware.
